items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Then we played one night at Ed Gauthier's country club which was one of the very few country clubs for Negroes in the States and owned by a Negro.

ctx.x: We played one week in Pittsburgh for a marathon dance which was the rage all over the country. How long it had been going on and how long it lasted after we left, I do not know. It was amazing to see some of the couples so tired that they would take turns to sleep on each others shoulders. We played slow number, fast ones and waltzes but the dancers never changed their pace which was the slowest of the slow drags.

From Pittsburgh we went to Cincinnati where we stayed for one week playing the Greystone Ballroom on a Sunday, Wednesday and Saturday for white dancers only. Then we played one night at Ed Gauthier's country club which was one of the very few country clubs for Negroes in the States and owned by a Negro. Gauthier had become a millionaire from the two gambling places that he owned in Cincinnati and the club which had golf links and a country swimming hole, was about six miles outside of Avondale a suburb of…

We stayed in Cincy two weeks and although I did not stay with my parents, I went to see them every day. Dickie Wells would always manage to get to my father's place before me because my ole man had learned to make home brew and always had a few bottles on ice. But when I arrived there, Dad would tell me that I was too late as Dickie had been there and drank all the cold beer.
